answer_1.quote: We propose COCOA for controllable codeswitched generation using a machine translation‑based model where the source and target languages are monolingual Hindi text and Hindi‑English CS text, respectively.

answer_2.quote: Semantic consistency with the source monolingual sentence is computed using BLEU scores between a reference CS sentence and the generated sentence. Attribute faithfulness for CMI is measured using two metrics: CMI acc and CMI corr. ... We also report perplexity of language models trained on the generated data.

answer_4.quote: We created a template that asks linguistic experts to assess model outputs on naturalness, semantic consistency and formality. Every CS sentence was evaluated along each of these dimensions by 3 human raters.
answer_4.guideline: Raters were shown a monolingual Hindi sentence and its generated code‑switched counterpart and asked to rate (1) how natural the mixed sentence sounds, (2) how well it captures the meaning of the Hindi sentence, and (3) which of two outputs is more formal.
